title: Chicago school gym: differential dry bulb
climate: Chicago, IL: cold winters, mixed summers. Freeze protection matters.
spec: Differential dry bulb (OA and RA temperature sensors).
Occupied minimum position 30% (4.4 V). No DCV.
Mixed air low limit 42°F, damper to MIN on freeze protection per the engineer.
Prove stroke and both cooling stages at checkout.

consequences.strategy: 30 days later: one sensor short of the spec. Free cooling decisions are made on OA alone. The engineer's commissioning report flags it.
consequences.MIN POS: 30 days later: the gym is either stuffy during a basketball game or the coil can't keep up.
consequences.MA LO SET: 30 days later: freeze protection kicks in at the wrong mixed-air temp.
consequences.FREEZE POS: 30 days later: the spec wanted ventilation held at MIN on freeze. You closed it, and the IAQ survey flags it.
consequences.LOW T LOCK: 30 days later: compressors running on 38°F days. Wasted energy and liquid slugging risk.
consequences.checkout: Y2 never proved. Stage 2 contactor was bad from the factory. Found on the first hot day.

note: Job specs are training values written to exercise the controller, not code-required values.
